patch.value:
Found by running the demos against a real 664-item workspace.

## The inconsistency

Three demos require an argument. Two validate it; the third does not:

```console
$ pm ts-starter search-demo
  pm-ts-starter: search-demo requires a --query (or positional query) argument.     # clear

$ pm ts-starter history-compact-demo
  pm-ts-starter: history-compact-demo requires an --id (or positional id) argument.  # clear

$ pm ts-starter plan-demo
  pm-ts-starter: `plan` demo failed (pm exited 2): {
    "type": "urn:pm-cli:error:invalid_argument_value",
    "detail": "pm plan show requires a plan id",
    ...20 more lines of nested JSON...
  }
```

`plan-demo` shells out as `pm --pm-path <path> plan show --depth standard --json` with no plan id, lets pm reject it, and forwards pm's entire error payload wrapped in its own.

## Why it matters here specifically

This package exists to **demonstrate correct SDK usage to extension authors**. Its own demos are the worked examples, so an inconsistency between them is a teaching defect rather than a cosmetic one: a reader comparing the three learns that argument validation is optional and that forwarding a nested error payload is an acceptable house style.

It is also the worst of the three to read. The useful sentence — `pm plan show requires a plan id` — is on line 4 of an embedded JSON blob, under a message that says the *demo* failed rather than that an argument is missing.

## Suggested fix

Validate up front, in the same voice as the siblings:

```
pm-ts-starter: plan-demo requires a --plan (or positional plan id) argument.
```

Or, if the demo is meant to be runnable with no arguments, have it resolve a plan itself (list plans, take the first, and say which it chose) so the zero-argument path demonstrates something rather than failing.

## Side effect worth knowing about

Because `plan-demo` places `--pm-path` **before** the subcommand, the forwarded payload also carries a malformed suggestion — `pm <path> --help`, the flag's value used as the command. That is an upstream defect in how pm derives the example, filed as [unbraind/pm-cli#984](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/984); it surfaces here because extensions build argv with global flags first. Validating the argument locally avoids forwarding it at all.

## What worked

The rest of the package behaved correctly against a real workspace: `info` reports name, version and the SDK target it was built against; `context-demo` produced a real context snapshot over 664 items; and the two sibling demos give exemplary usage errors — which is precisely why the third stands out.
